title: Prompt engineering and CLI overhaul
description:
# Prompt Engineering and CLI Overhaul

## Context

Two independent external reviews (REVIEW.md and research.md) plus hands-on debugging identified 15 concrete improvements to ralph's prompt templates, CLI flag usage, and invocation pipeline. The full analysis is in RECOMMENDED-CHANGES.md at the project root. This epic implements all recommendations in dependency order.

The reviews surfaced three categories of issue:
* Underutilised Claude Code CLI capabilities (--bare, --append-system-prompt-file, per-type --max-turns, --disallowedTools, --max-budget-usd)
* Prompt engineering defects (commit contradiction, suboptimal section ordering, negative-only rules, no failure inoculation)
* Missing outer loop mechanics (outcome verification, error-type-aware escalation, cumulative retry history, structured handoff)

## Approach

Implement in dependency order from RECOMMENDED-CHANGES.md §Implementation Order. Template-only changes land first (low risk, immediate effect), then CLI pipeline changes (--bare foundation), then features that build on the new pipeline (per-type turns/timeouts, tool scoping, outcome verification).

Key architectural decisions:
* All stable behavioural rules move to a new ralph-system-prompt.md file loaded via --append-system-prompt-file, NOT into the project CLAUDE.md (which --bare skips)
* Per-type turns, timeouts, and tool scoping are configured via associative arrays in config.sh with a dispatch function, NOT per-file constants
* invoke_claude() gains optional parameters (max_turns, timeout, disallowed_tools) that override globals when present, preserving backward compatibility
* The @turns and @timeout playlist annotations already exist and will continue to override per-type defaults

## Critical files

* lib/invoke.sh — _invoke_claude_once (line 98), invoke_claude (line 51), escalate_model (line 80)
* lib/invoke_retry.sh — augment_prompt_with_failure_context (line 12), diagnose_exit_code (line 58)
* lib/prompt.sh — build_prompt (line 12), build_raw_prompt (line 43), format_branch_instructions (line 98), format_commit_rule (line 130)
* lib/prompt_context.sh — format_prior_task_context (line 14), clear_task_handoff (line 26)
* lib/task_outcome.sh — capture_task_handoff (line 49), handle_task_outcome (line 12)
* lib/config.sh — all default globals
* lib/playlist.sh — playlist_execute_bead (line 150), playlist_execute_prompt (line 179)
* lib/gates.sh — gate_expand_tag (line 33)
* templates/prompt_bead.txt, templates/prompt_raw.txt, templates/retry_context.txt
* templates/branch_playlist.txt
* templates/gate_*.txt (5 gate templates)

## Verification

After each task:
* ralph --dry-run (verify no parse errors)
* ralph --dry-run --playlist test-playlists/mixed.playlist (playlist dry-run still works)
* Spot-check modified templates by reading them and confirming placeholder substitution is correct
* For invoke.sh changes: run a single bead to confirm invocation succeeds

title: Fix commit contradiction in playlist branch template
description:
## What to implement

The playlist branch template (templates/branch_playlist.txt) always says "Commit directly on <branch>" regardless of AUTO_COMMIT setting. When AUTO_COMMIT=false (the playlist default), this contradicts Rule 4 in the bead prompt which says "Do NOT commit." Claude receives both instructions in the same prompt and follows whichever it weights more heavily, producing inconsistent commit behaviour.

Fix the template so the commit instruction is conditional on AUTO_COMMIT.

## Files to modify

* templates/branch_playlist.txt — add {{COMMIT_INSTRUCTION}} placeholder replacing the hardcoded "Commit directly" line
* lib/prompt.sh — update format_branch_instructions() (line 98-124) in the playlist:* case (line 101-105) to compute and pass COMMIT_INSTRUCTION based on AUTO_COMMIT

## Implementation detail

1. In templates/branch_playlist.txt, replace:
   "Commit directly on {{BRANCH}}. Merging is a separate manual step."
   with:
   "{{COMMIT_INSTRUCTION}}"

2. In lib/prompt.sh format_branch_instructions(), update the playlist:* case:

```bash
playlist:*)
    local branch="${branch_ctx#playlist:}"
    local commit_instr
    if [[ "$AUTO_COMMIT" == true ]]; then
        commit_instr="Commit directly on \`$branch\`. Merging is a separate manual step."
    else
        commit_instr="Leave changes staged or unstaged — the outer loop handles commits."
    fi
    render_template "$TEMPLATES_DIR/branch_playlist.txt" \
        "BRANCH=$branch" \
        "COMMIT_INSTRUCTION=$commit_instr"
    ;;
```

## Patterns to follow

* render_template() usage pattern from lib/utils.sh:180-190 — {{KEY}} placeholder substitution
* Conditional formatting pattern already used by format_commit_rule() at lib/prompt.sh:130-136

## Acceptance criteria

* When AUTO_COMMIT=false (playlist default): branch section says "Leave changes staged or unstaged"
* When AUTO_COMMIT=true: branch section says "Commit directly on <branch>"
* No contradiction exists between branch section and Rule 4 in either mode
* ralph --dry-run --playlist test-playlists/mixed.playlist still works (no parse errors)

title: Add tool scoping per prompt type via --disallowedTools
description:
## What to implement

Use Claude Code's --disallowedTools flag to restrict tool access per invocation type. A #REVIEW gate that physically cannot call Write/Edit cannot make unintended changes regardless of prompt instructions. This is defence-in-depth — the same pattern Claude Code uses for its own Explore sub-agent.

## Files to modify

* lib/config.sh — add PROMPT_TYPE_DISALLOWED_TOOLS associative array
* lib/invoke.sh — update _invoke_claude_once() (line 98-147) to pass --disallowedTools when set
* lib/playlist.sh — playlist_execute_prompt() (line 179) sets tool scope based on gate type

## Implementation detail

### config.sh — tool scope lookup

```bash
# Per-prompt-type disallowed tools. Empty string = no restrictions.
declare -A PROMPT_TYPE_DISALLOWED_TOOLS=(
    [gate_review]="Bash,Write,Edit,NotebookEdit"
    [gate_smoke_test]="Write,Edit,NotebookEdit"
    [playlist_validate]="Bash,Write,Edit"
    [playlist_create]="Bash,Write,Edit"
)
```

Add helper:
```bash
get_prompt_disallowed_tools() {
    local type="$1"
    echo "${PROMPT_TYPE_DISALLOWED_TOOLS[$type]:-}"
}
```

### invoke.sh — pass the flag

In _invoke_claude_once(), build the claude command dynamically. Before the invocation, check if invocation_disallowed_tools is set:

```bash
local -a claude_args=(
    -p "$prompt"
    --bare
    --append-system-prompt-file "$RALPH_DIR/ralph-system-prompt.md"
    --dangerously-skip-permissions
    --model "$MODEL"
    --output-format stream-json
    --max-turns "${invocation_max_turns:-$MAX_TURNS}"
    --verbose
)

if [[ -n "${invocation_disallowed_tools:-}" ]]; then
    claude_args+=(--disallowedTools "$invocation_disallowed_tools")
fi
```

This means _invoke_claude_once needs to be updated to use an array for command args instead of a single long line. The caller sets invocation_disallowed_tools before calling invoke_claude().

### playlist.sh — set tool scope for gates

In playlist_execute_prompt() (line 179), after gate expansion:

```bash
if [[ -n "${playlist_line_gate_tag:-}" ]]; then
    local gate_key="gate_$(echo "$playlist_line_gate_tag" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
    invocation_disallowed_tools=$(get_prompt_disallowed_tools "$gate_key")
fi
```

For non-gate prompts, invocation_disallowed_tools stays empty (no restrictions).

## Patterns to follow

* Associative array lookup pattern from PROMPT_TYPE_TURNS (added by ralph-046.4)
* invocation_* global pattern for per-call overrides
* Array-based command building is cleaner than string interpolation for optional flags

## Acceptance criteria

* #REVIEW gate invocations include --disallowedTools "Bash,Write,Edit,NotebookEdit"
* #SMOKE_TEST gate invocations include --disallowedTools "Write,Edit,NotebookEdit"
* Bead and raw prompt invocations have no tool restrictions (default)
* The --disallowedTools flag is omitted entirely when no restrictions apply (not passed as empty string)
* ralph --dry-run still works
* invocation_disallowed_tools is cleared between invocations (no leakage)

title: Error-type-aware escalation and cumulative failure history
description:
## What to implement

Two related changes to the retry/escalation pipeline:

1. Classify failure types before deciding whether to retry same model, escalate, backoff, or decompose. Currently all failures trigger model escalation regardless of type — timeouts get thrown at opus which will also time out.
2. Pass cumulative failure history across retries so attempt 3 knows about attempts 1 and 2.

## Files to modify

* lib/invoke.sh — rewrite escalate_model() (line 80) and invoke_claude() retry loop (line 51) to classify failure type before deciding action
* lib/invoke_retry.sh — rewrite augment_prompt_with_failure_context() (line 12) to accumulate history; update extract_failure_tail() if needed
* templates/retry_context.txt — add FAILURE_HISTORY and TASK_ID placeholders, add Pattern Analysis section

## Implementation detail

### Failure classification

Add a function classify_failure() in invoke.sh or invoke_retry.sh:

```bash
classify_failure() {
    local exit_code="$1"
    case $exit_code in
        124)    echo "timeout" ;;
        137)    echo "oom_killed" ;;
        1)      echo "general_error" ;;
        2)      echo "misuse" ;;
        *)      echo "unknown" ;;
    esac
}
```

### Escalation decision matrix

Replace the blanket escalate_model() call in invoke_claude() (line 68) with type-aware routing:

```bash
local failure_type
failure_type=$(classify_failure "$invoke_exit")

case "$failure_type" in
    timeout)
        # Don't escalate model — task may be too large
        log "Timeout: retrying same model with reduced scope guidance"
        ;;
    oom_killed)
        # Don't escalate — instruct shorter output
        log "OOM: retrying same model with shorter output guidance"
        ;;
    general_error)
        # This is where model escalation helps
        escalate_model "$original_model"
        ;;
    *)
        escalate_model "$original_model"
        ;;
esac
```

### Cumulative failure history

Add a FAILURE_HISTORY variable that accumulates across retries:

```bash
# In invoke_claude(), before the retry loop:
local failure_history=""

# After each failure, append to history:
failure_history+="Attempt $attempt: $(diagnose_exit_code $invoke_exit) — $MODEL\n"
```

Pass FAILURE_HISTORY to augment_prompt_with_failure_context().

### Updated retry_context.txt template

```
## RETRY CONTEXT (attempt {{ATTEMPT}}/{{MAX_RETRIES}})

### Failure History
{{FAILURE_HISTORY}}

### Most Recent Failure
* Exit code: {{EXIT_CODE}}
* Diagnosis: {{DIAGNOSIS}}

### Last output before failure
{{LAST_OUTPUT}}

### Adapt Your Approach
* If the issue was a timeout: work in smaller steps, do less per invocation.
* If the issue was context overflow: produce shorter output, avoid large file reads.
* If the issue was an API error: this may be transient, try the same approach.
* If the issue was a tool error: try an alternative approach to achieve the same goal.
* Do NOT repeat the exact same sequence of actions that failed.
* If multiple failures share a root cause (e.g., task too large for time budget), consider decomposing: create 2-3 sub-beads with `br create` and release the parent with `br update {{TASK_ID}} --status open`.
```

### augment_prompt_with_failure_context() changes

Update to accept and render FAILURE_HISTORY and TASK_ID:

```bash
augment_prompt_with_failure_context() {
    local exit_code="$1"
    local attempt="$2"
    local failure_history="$3"
    local task_id="${tid:-unknown}"

    local diagnosis last_output retry_block
    diagnosis=$(diagnose_exit_code "$exit_code")
    last_output=$(extract_failure_tail)
    retry_block=$(render_template "$TEMPLATES_DIR/retry_context.txt" \
        "ATTEMPT=$((attempt + 1))" \
        "MAX_RETRIES=$MAX_RETRIES" \
        "EXIT_CODE=$exit_code" \
        "DIAGNOSIS=$diagnosis" \
        "LAST_OUTPUT=$last_output" \
        "FAILURE_HISTORY=$failure_history" \
        "TASK_ID=$task_id")
    prompt="${prompt}${retry_block}"
}
```

## Patterns to follow

* diagnose_exit_code() at lib/invoke_retry.sh:58-67 — case statement on exit codes
* render_template() at lib/utils.sh:180-190
* The retry loop pattern at lib/invoke.sh:55-72

## Acceptance criteria

* Timeout failures (exit 124) do NOT trigger model escalation
* General errors (exit 1) DO trigger model escalation
* Attempt 3's retry context includes history of attempts 1 and 2
* The FAILURE_HISTORY block shows "Attempt N: diagnosis — model" for each prior failure
* The Pattern Analysis section suggests decomposition when failures share a root cause
* ralph --dry-run still works

title: Add outcome-based verification to the outer loop
description:
## What to implement

After each invocation, verify outcomes mechanically rather than trusting Claude's prose claims. Agents can produce no-op implementations that pass quality checks without addressing requirements. The outer loop should check exit codes, git diffs, and file existence.

Add a verify_outcome() function called after each invocation that performs type-specific checks.

## Files to modify

* lib/task_outcome.sh — add verify_outcome() function, call it from handle_task_outcome() (line 12)
* lib/playlist.sh — call verify_outcome() after prompt execution in playlist_execute_prompt() (line 179)

## Files to create

* lib/outcome_verify.sh (NEW) — outcome verification functions, sourced by loader.sh

## Implementation detail

### lib/outcome_verify.sh (new file)

```bash
# outcome_verify.sh — Mechanical verification of invocation outcomes.
#
# verify_outcome(): dispatch to type-specific checks after each invocation.
# Returns 0 if outcome verified, 1 if verification failed.

verify_outcome() {
    local type="$1"    # bead, gate_review, gate_smoke_test, etc.
    local tid="${2:-}"  # bead ID, empty for prompts

    case "$type" in
        bead)           verify_bead_outcome "$tid" ;;
        gate_review)    verify_review_outcome ;;
        gate_refactor)  verify_refactor_outcome ;;
        gate_document)  verify_document_outcome ;;
        report)         verify_report_outcome ;;
        *)              return 0 ;;  # no verification for unknown types
    esac
}

verify_bead_outcome() {
    local tid="$1"
    # Check bead actually closed
    local status
    status=$(get_bead_status "$tid")
    if [[ "$status" != "closed" ]]; then
        log "WARNING: Bead $tid not closed after invocation (status: $status)"
        return 1
    fi
    # Check something actually changed
    local files_changed
    files_changed=$(git diff --stat HEAD~1 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
    if [[ "$files_changed" -eq 0 ]]; then
        log "WARNING: Bead $tid closed but no files changed in last commit"
    fi
    return 0
}

verify_review_outcome() {
    # Review gates should NOT modify files
    local dirty_files
    dirty_files=$(git diff --stat 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
    if [[ "$dirty_files" -gt 0 ]]; then
        log "WARNING: Review gate modified files (expected read-only)"
        git diff --stat 2>/dev/null | head -5 | while read -r line; do
            log "  $line"
        done
    fi
    return 0
}

verify_refactor_outcome() {
    # Refactor gates should leave tests passing
    # Only check if a test runner is configured
    # For now, just warn if there are uncommitted changes
    return 0
}

verify_document_outcome() {
    # Document gates should have modified docs/
    local docs_changed
    docs_changed=$(git diff --name-only 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^docs/' || true)
    if [[ "$docs_changed" -eq 0 ]]; then
        log "WARNING: Document gate completed but no docs/ files modified"
    fi
    return 0
}

verify_report_outcome() {
    # Report should have created the report file
    # The report path is in the prompt — check .ralph/reports/ exists
    if [[ -d ".ralph/reports" ]]; then
        local report_count
        report_count=$(find .ralph/reports -name "*.md" -newer .ralph/state 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
        if [[ "$report_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
            log "WARNING: Report invocation completed but no report file found"
        fi
    fi
    return 0
}
```

### Integration points

In lib/task_outcome.sh handle_task_outcome() (line 12), after check_bead_status:
```bash
verify_outcome "bead" "$tid"
```

In lib/playlist.sh playlist_execute_prompt() (line 179), after invoke_claude succeeds:
```bash
if [[ -n "${playlist_line_gate_tag:-}" ]]; then
    local gate_key="gate_$(echo "$playlist_line_gate_tag" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
    verify_outcome "$gate_key"
else
    verify_outcome "raw"
fi
```

### loader.sh

Add `source "$LIB_DIR/outcome_verify.sh"` after task_outcome.sh in the load order.

## Patterns to follow

* get_bead_status() from lib/utils_beads.sh — query bead status
* log() from lib/utils.sh — consistent logging
* File size limit: keep under 200 lines (CLAUDE.md rule)
* Function naming: verify_* prefix for verification functions

## Acceptance criteria

* verify_outcome() is called after every bead execution and gate execution
* Bead verification checks that status is closed and files were changed
* Review gate verification warns if files were modified
* Document gate verification warns if docs/ was not modified
* All verifications are WARNING-level (log only, don't block execution)
* outcome_verify.sh is under 200 lines
* ralph --dry-run still works (verification is skipped in dry-run since no invocations occur)

title: Add decomposition prompt type for repeated failures
description:
## What to implement

When a bead fails twice consecutively (2 timeouts, or 2 failures of any type after all retries exhausted), trigger a decomposition prompt instead of giving up. The decomposition prompt instructs Claude to break the oversized task into 2-4 sub-beads and release the parent — turning a failure loop into productive work.

## Files to create

* templates/prompt_decompose.txt (NEW) — decomposition prompt template

## Files to modify

* lib/invoke.sh — add logic after invoke_claude() exhausts retries to check consecutive failure count and trigger decomposition
* lib/prompt.sh — add build_decompose_prompt() function
* lib/config.sh — add DECOMPOSE_AFTER_FAILURES=2 default

## Implementation detail

### templates/prompt_decompose.txt

```
You are decomposing a task that has failed {{FAILURE_COUNT}} times in the ralph autonomous loop.

<task>
ID: {{TASK_ID}}
{{DETAILS}}
</task>

<failure_history>
{{FAILURE_HISTORY}}
</failure_history>

<instructions>
1. Analyse why this task is too large or complex for a single invocation.
2. Break it into 2-4 sub-tasks, each completable in under 10 minutes.
3. Create each sub-task with br create:
   br create --title "..." --type task --parent {{TASK_ID}} --description "..."
4. Release the parent task:
   br update {{TASK_ID}} --status open
5. The outer loop will pick up the sub-tasks in subsequent iterations.
</instructions>

<rules>
Each sub-task must be independently testable.
Sub-tasks should be ordered by dependency (foundational first).
Add dependencies between sub-tasks with br dep add <blocker> <blocked>.
Do NOT implement anything — only decompose and create beads.
</rules>
```

### lib/prompt.sh — build_decompose_prompt()

```bash
build_decompose_prompt() {
    local task_id="$1"
    local details="$2"
    local failure_history="$3"
    local failure_count="$4"

    prompt=$(render_template "$TEMPLATES_DIR/prompt_decompose.txt" \
        "TASK_ID=$task_id" \
        "DETAILS=$details" \
        "FAILURE_HISTORY=$failure_history" \
        "FAILURE_COUNT=$failure_count")
}
```

### Integration in the main loop

After invoke_claude() returns 1 (all retries exhausted), check if consecutive_failures >= DECOMPOSE_AFTER_FAILURES. If so:

```bash
if [[ $consecutive_failures -ge $DECOMPOSE_AFTER_FAILURES ]]; then
    log "Triggering task decomposition after $consecutive_failures consecutive failures"
    build_decompose_prompt "$tid" "$task_details" "$failure_history" "$consecutive_failures"
    invocation_max_turns=$(get_prompt_turns "decompose")
    invoke_claude && {
        log "Task $tid decomposed into sub-tasks"
        consecutive_failures=0
    }
fi
```

The consecutive_failures counter needs to be tracked — increment when invoke_claude fails on the same tid, reset when a different tid is attempted or when any invocation succeeds.

### Per-type limits

Add to the PROMPT_TYPE_TURNS and PROMPT_TYPE_TIMEOUT arrays (from ralph-046.4):
```bash
[decompose]=10  # turns — needs to analyse and create beads
```
Timeout: 5 minutes.

## Patterns to follow

* build_prompt() / build_raw_prompt() pattern in lib/prompt.sh
* render_template() in lib/utils.sh:180-190
* The invocation pattern: build prompt → set limits → invoke_claude()

## Acceptance criteria

* After 2 consecutive failures on the same bead, decomposition prompt fires
* Decomposition prompt instructs Claude to create sub-beads, not implement
* Parent bead is released (status open) after decomposition
* The outer loop picks up sub-beads in subsequent iterations via br ready
* DECOMPOSE_AFTER_FAILURES is configurable in config.sh
* ralph --dry-run still works

title: Add gate scope caps and conditional orientation depth
description:
## What to implement

Two template-level improvements:

1. Gate scope caps: limit how many issues a gate can create and how many files the #REFACTOR gate can modify. Prevents 15-bead creation events that distort the playlist.
2. Conditional orientation depth: use a shortened orientation for sequential playlist beads where prior context exists and the previous bead closed successfully. Saves 2-3 turns.

## Files to modify

* templates/gate_smoke_test.txt — add scope limit paragraph
* templates/gate_completeness_scan.txt — add scope limit paragraph
* templates/gate_review.txt — add scope limit paragraph
* templates/gate_refactor.txt — add scope limit paragraph with file cap
* templates/gate_document.txt — add scope limit paragraph
* templates/prompt_bead.txt — add conditional orientation variant
* lib/prompt_context.sh — add format_orientation() function that selects full vs quick based on context

## Implementation detail

### Gate scope caps

Add this block to each gate template (before the self-healing / bead creation instructions):

```
## Scope Limit
If this analysis identifies more than 10 distinct issues, prioritise the top 5 by severity and create beads only for those. List the remainder in your output for future reference.
```

For gate_refactor.txt specifically, add additionally:
```
If more than 10 files were modified in the session, focus on the top 5 by complexity.
If you cannot complete all planned refactoring within this invocation, revert uncommitted changes and create beads for the remaining work.
```

### Conditional orientation

Add a new template templates/orientation_quick.txt:

```
## Orientation (Quick)
The previous bead closed successfully. Run `git diff --stat` to confirm the scope of recent changes matches the Prior Task Context above. If it matches, proceed to implementation. If it does not match, run full orientation: `git diff`, `git show HEAD`, `git log --oneline -5`.
```

The existing full orientation stays in prompt_bead.txt as the default.

In lib/prompt_context.sh, add:

```bash
format_orientation() {
    if [[ -n "${LAST_TASK_ID:-}" && "${_last_bead_closed:-false}" == "true" ]]; then
        cat "$TEMPLATES_DIR/orientation_quick.txt"
    else
        cat "$TEMPLATES_DIR/orientation_full.txt"
    fi
}
```

This requires extracting the current Orientation section from prompt_bead.txt into templates/orientation_full.txt, and using {{ORIENTATION}} placeholder in the bead template.

In lib/prompt.sh build_prompt(), add:
```bash
local orientation
orientation=$(format_orientation)
```
And pass "ORIENTATION=$orientation" to render_template.

Update templates/prompt_bead.txt to use {{ORIENTATION}} instead of inline orientation text.

The _last_bead_closed flag needs to be set in handle_task_outcome() when bead_status is "closed":
```bash
_last_bead_closed=true   # in the closed case
_last_bead_closed=false  # in all other cases
```

## Patterns to follow

* format_prior_task_context() at lib/prompt_context.sh:14 — conditional section formatting
* Template extraction pattern: content moves from inline to templates/ file

## Acceptance criteria

* All 5 gate templates have a "Scope Limit" section
* #REFACTOR gate has an additional file count cap
* Sequential playlist beads with prior context get quick orientation
* First bead in a session or after a failed bead gets full orientation
* Both orientation variants tell Claude how to check git state
* ralph --dry-run still works

title: Add --max-budget-usd per invocation and emphasis inflation audit
description:
## What to implement

Two final hardening changes:

1. Per-invocation cost ceiling via --max-budget-usd. Defence in depth alongside max-turns and timeouts.
2. Audit all templates for MUST, ALWAYS, CRITICAL, ALL CAPS emphasis markers and replace with clear conditional logic. Claude 4.x evaluates logical necessity, not emphasis.

## Files to modify

* lib/config.sh — add PROMPT_TYPE_BUDGET associative array
* lib/invoke.sh — pass --max-budget-usd when set (in the claude_args array from ralph-046.10)
* All templates in templates/ — audit and de-emphasise

## Implementation detail

### Per-invocation cost ceiling

Add to config.sh:
```bash
declare -A PROMPT_TYPE_BUDGET=(
    [bead]="2.00"
    [raw]="2.00"
    [gate_smoke_test]="1.00"
    [gate_completeness_scan]="1.00"
    [gate_review]="1.00"
    [gate_refactor]="1.00"
    [gate_document]="1.00"
    [report]="0.50"
    [summary]="0.50"
    [playlist_create]="0.50"
    [playlist_validate]="0.50"
    [decompose]="0.50"
)
```

Add helper:
```bash
get_prompt_budget() {
    local type="$1"
    echo "${PROMPT_TYPE_BUDGET[$type]:-}"
}
```

In invoke.sh, add to the claude_args array (from ralph-046.10):
```bash
if [[ -n "${invocation_budget:-}" ]]; then
    claude_args+=(--max-budget-usd "$invocation_budget")
fi
```

Callers set invocation_budget before invoke_claude():
```bash
invocation_budget=$(get_prompt_budget "bead")
```

### Emphasis audit

Search all templates for: MUST, ALWAYS, CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, NEVER, ALL CAPS phrases, exclamation marks used for emphasis.

For each occurrence:
* If it's conveying a genuine constraint: rewrite as a clear conditional statement. Example: "You MUST close the bead before exiting" → "Close the bead before exiting. The outer loop depends on the bead status to track progress."
* If it's generic emphasis: remove the emphasis marker. Example: "IMPORTANT — adapt your approach:" → "Adapt your approach:"
* If it's a specific negative targeting a failure mode: keep it, it's valid (see ralph-046.6)

Expected files to audit:
* templates/prompt_bead.txt
* templates/prompt_raw.txt
* templates/retry_context.txt
* templates/prompt_report.txt
* templates/gate_refactor.txt (longest template, most likely to have emphasis)
* ralph-system-prompt.md (created by ralph-046.3)

## Patterns to follow

* PROMPT_TYPE_* associative array pattern from ralph-046.4
* invocation_* global pattern for per-call overrides

## Acceptance criteria

* --max-budget-usd is passed for all prompt types that have a budget configured

title: Per-prompt-type max-turns and timeout calibration
description:
## What to implement

Replace the blanket MAX_TURNS=500 and TIMEOUT_MINUTES=10 with per-prompt-type values. The current 500-turn ceiling is functionally unlimited — Anthropic recommends 5-10 for moderate tasks. Similarly, a 10-minute timeout is too generous for smoke tests and too tight for complex refactoring.

Add a dispatch mechanism so each prompt builder can request its appropriate limits, while playlist @turns and @timeout annotations continue to override.

## Files to modify

* lib/config.sh — add PROMPT_TYPE_TURNS and PROMPT_TYPE_TIMEOUT associative arrays with defaults
* lib/invoke.sh — update invoke_claude() (line 51) and _invoke_claude_once() (line 98) to accept optional max_turns and timeout_secs parameters that override globals
* lib/prompt.sh — build_prompt() (line 12) and build_raw_prompt() (line 43) set invocation_max_turns and invocation_timeout before invoke_claude is called
* lib/playlist.sh — playlist_execute_bead() (line 150) and playlist_execute_prompt() (line 179) set limits based on prompt type, gate type, or annotation overrides
* lib/gates.sh — gate_expand_tag() (line 33) returns recommended turns/timeout alongside the expanded text

## Implementation detail

### config.sh — add lookup arrays

```bash
# Per-prompt-type turn limits. Overridden by @turns annotation.
declare -A PROMPT_TYPE_TURNS=(
    [bead]=25
    [raw]=25
    [gate_smoke_test]=10
    [gate_completeness_scan]=10
    [gate_review]=10
    [gate_refactor]=30
    [gate_document]=15
    [report]=5
    [summary]=5
    [playlist_create]=5
    [playlist_validate]=5
)

# Per-prompt-type timeouts in minutes. Overridden by @timeout annotation.
declare -A PROMPT_TYPE_TIMEOUT=(
    [bead]=15
    [raw]=15
    [gate_smoke_test]=5
    [gate_completeness_scan]=5
    [gate_review]=5
    [gate_refactor]=15
    [gate_document]=10
    [report]=3
    [summary]=3
    [playlist_create]=3
    [playlist_validate]=3
)
```

Add a helper function to resolve the effective limit:
```bash
get_prompt_turns() {
    local type="$1"
    echo "${PROMPT_TYPE_TURNS[$type]:-$MAX_TURNS}"
}
get_prompt_timeout() {
    local type="$1"
    echo "${PROMPT_TYPE_TIMEOUT[$type]:-$TIMEOUT_MINUTES}"
}
```

### invoke.sh — accept per-invocation overrides

Change invoke_claude() to read from globals set by the caller:
* invocation_max_turns (if set, overrides MAX_TURNS for this call)
* invocation_timeout_secs (if set, overrides TIMEOUT_SECS for this call)

In _invoke_claude_once(), use ${invocation_max_turns:-$MAX_TURNS} and ${invocation_timeout_secs:-$TIMEOUT_SECS} in the claude command and timeout prefix.

### Caller pattern

Each prompt builder sets the globals before invoke_claude():
```bash
invocation_max_turns=$(get_prompt_turns "bead")
invocation_timeout_secs=$(($(get_prompt_timeout "bead") * 60))
```

For retries, add +5 to the original type's turns:
```bash
invocation_max_turns=$((invocation_max_turns + 5))
```

Playlist annotations (@turns, @timeout) already override via apply_line_overrides() in lib/playlist_annotations.sh:64-80, which sets MAX_TURNS and TIMEOUT_SECS globally. These should take precedence over per-type defaults. The resolution order is: annotation override > per-type default > global default.

## Patterns to follow

* apply_line_overrides() / restore_line_overrides() pattern in lib/playlist_annotations.sh:64-93 — save/restore around invocation
* Associative array usage: bash declare -A

## Acceptance criteria

* Default MAX_TURNS is no longer 500 for any prompt type
* Each prompt type gets its own turns and timeout as specified in the table
* Playlist @turns and @timeout annotations still override per-type defaults
* ralph --dry-run still works
* The global MAX_TURNS=500 in config.sh becomes a fallback only (used when prompt type is unknown)

description:
## What to implement

Replace the 200-word prose handoff with a structured JSON file (.ralph/handoff.json) that the next invocation reads via its Read tool. The current truncation loses structural decisions, naming conventions, and partial implementation details when a bead modifies many files.

## Files to modify

## Implementation detail

### lib/task_outcome.sh — capture_task_handoff()

Replace current implementation (line 49-53) with:

```bash
capture_task_handoff() {
    local tid="$1"
    LAST_TASK_ID="$tid"

    local summary files_changed commit_hash
    summary=$(extract_last_assistant_text "${INVOKE_LOG:-}")
    files_changed=$(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 2>/dev/null | jq -R -s 'split("\n") | map(select(. != ""))' 2>/dev/null || echo "[]")
    commit_hash=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")

    # Write structured handoff
    jq -n \
        --arg bead_id "$tid" \
        --arg status "closed" \
        --argjson files_changed "$files_changed" \
        --arg summary "${summary:0:500}" \
        --arg commit "$commit_hash" \
        '{bead_id: $bead_id, status: $status, files_changed: $files_changed, summary: $summary, commit: $commit}' \
        > .ralph/handoff.json

    # Keep LAST_TASK_SUMMARY for backward compat (used by progress display)
    LAST_TASK_SUMMARY="$summary"
}
```

Key changes:
* Writes .ralph/handoff.json with bead_id, status, files_changed array, summary (truncated to 500 chars not 200 words), and commit hash
* Uses jq for safe JSON construction (handles special characters in summary)
* Keeps LAST_TASK_SUMMARY set for backward compatibility with progress display

            "LAST_TASK_ID=$LAST_TASK_ID" \

            "LAST_TASK_ID=$LAST_TASK_ID" \

description:
Report ref: R1. Estimated savings: $15-20/run (150-200 turns).

Every bead in ralph's loop starts with an empty context window — no memory of what the previous bead did. The first 5-10 turns of each task are spent re-exploring the codebase. This bead gives the next agent two complementary handoff channels:

* **Part A — Claimed summary:** what the *previous* agent said it did (captured from its own stream-log output). Cheap, commit-state-agnostic, but reflects agent claims not ground truth.
* **Part B — Ground-truth orientation:** instructions telling the *next* agent how to verify that against the actual repo state (`git status` → branch on dirty/clean → `git diff` or `git show HEAD`). Costs 2-3 tool calls in the agent's first turn, but reflects reality.

Both are required. Part A alone is untrustworthy (agent might have lied about what it did). Part B alone is uniform but misses intent — the "why" of what changed. Together they cover both playlist mode (AUTO_COMMIT=false, prior work sits uncommitted in the working tree) and standalone mode (AUTO_COMMIT=true, prior work is in HEAD).

## Why both parts are needed

In playlist mode, AUTO_COMMIT=false is the default (see validate_playlist_args in lib/args.sh). Beads in a playlist typically do NOT commit per-task; commits happen at > checkpoint prompts. This means for most beads in a playlist run, the prior bead's work is invisible to `git log` — it's sitting uncommitted in the working tree, only visible via `git diff` / `git status`.

Any handoff strategy that assumes committed work is broken for ralph's primary execution mode. The orientation recipe (Part B) must branch on commit state to work correctly.

Part A (stream-log summary) is commit-state-agnostic by construction — it captures what the agent said regardless of whether anything got committed. This is its main virtue over a pure git-based approach. But it captures claims, not facts, so Part B is the verification layer.

## Part A — Claimed summary (existing spec, refined)

Capture a ~200-word excerpt from the previous invocation's stream-json log and inject it into the next prompt as a `## Prior Task Context` section.

Implementation:
* In lib/task_outcome.sh handle_task_outcome(), after a task closes (status=closed), extract the last assistant text block from $INVOKE_LOG (the stream-json path already set by lib/invoke.sh). Store in a global LAST_TASK_SUMMARY.
* Extraction uses jq over the JSONL — find the last message with role=assistant and content type=text, take the text, collapse whitespace, truncate to ~200 words. If the stream log is missing or empty, set LAST_TASK_SUMMARY="" and move on silently.
* Also capture a second global LAST_TASK_ID = the ID of the just-closed bead, for use in Part B's orientation section.
* In lib/prompt.sh build_prompt(), if LAST_TASK_SUMMARY is non-empty, render a new `## Prior Task Context` section (from a new template fragment, e.g. templates/prior_task_context.txt) with LAST_TASK_ID and LAST_TASK_SUMMARY. Inject it after `## Your Task` in templates/prompt_bead.txt via a new {{PRIOR_TASK_CONTEXT}} placeholder (empty string when no prior task).
* Also inject LAST_TASK_SUMMARY into build_raw_prompt() for > prompt-type playlist lines.
* Clear LAST_TASK_SUMMARY and LAST_TASK_ID after injecting — retries of the same task should NOT see stale context.
* First task in a session: LAST_TASK_SUMMARY is empty, the section is omitted.

## Part B — Ground-truth orientation (new)

Add a static `## Orientation` section to templates/prompt_bead.txt (no template variable — same instructions for every bead). The section tells the agent to check the repo state before implementing, and branches on commit state so it works in both playlist and standalone mode:

  ## Orientation
  Before implementing, orient yourself to what the previous bead left behind:

  1. Run `git status` to see if the working tree is dirty.
     * If dirty: run `git diff` — this is the previous bead's uncommitted work in playlist mode (AUTO_COMMIT=false by default). Read it before making changes so you understand what's in flight.
     * If clean: run `git log --oneline -5` and `git show HEAD` — the previous bead's work is in the most recent commit(s). Read the diff to see what changed.
  2. If a `## Prior Task Context` section appears above, treat it as the previous agent's CLAIM about what it did. Use `git diff` / `git show HEAD` to verify that claim against ground truth before trusting it.
  3. Do not re-explore files that the orientation already showed you changed. Start from the established state.

This section is STATIC — identical for every bead, rendered verbatim. No {{PLACEHOLDER}} needed. It goes in templates/prompt_bead.txt between `## Your Task` and `## Rules` (or between `## Prior Task Context` and `## Branch` — designer's choice, but Orientation must come BEFORE Rules so the agent reads it before starting implementation).

## Template changes

templates/prompt_bead.txt gains two new sections in this order:
  ## Your Task
  {{PRIOR_TASK_CONTEXT}}       ← Part A, empty string on first task
  ## Orientation               ← Part B, static text (see above)
  ## Branch
  {{BRANCH_SECTION}}
  ## Rules
  ...

A new templates/prior_task_context.txt fragment holds the Part A section body:
  ## Prior Task Context
  The previous bead ({{LAST_TASK_ID}}) closed with this summary from its own final output:

  {{LAST_TASK_SUMMARY}}

  Treat this as a CLAIM, not ground truth — verify with `git diff` / `git show HEAD` (see Orientation below).

When LAST_TASK_SUMMARY is empty, build_prompt() sets {{PRIOR_TASK_CONTEXT}}="" so the section vanishes cleanly.

## Implementation — new helper

Extract the jq-over-stream-log into a named helper to keep handle_task_outcome readable. Per the updated CLAUDE.md naming convention (get_* spawns a subprocess, extract_* operates on pre-fetched data), this one is a file read with a jq filter — name it `extract_last_assistant_text()` taking the log path as its argument. It does not spawn br. If the jq filter exceeds ~3 lines, move the filter to templates/last_assistant_text.jq and load it with `jq -f`.

## Acceptance criteria

Part A:
* After a bead closes, LAST_TASK_SUMMARY and LAST_TASK_ID are populated from the just-finished invocation's stream log.
* The next invocation's prompt includes `## Prior Task Context` with LAST_TASK_ID and the summary text.
* Both globals are cleared after the prompt is built, so a retry of the same task does not see stale context.
* First task in a session: no `## Prior Task Context` section (empty-string substitution).
* If the stream log is missing, empty, or parse-fails: LAST_TASK_SUMMARY="", no crash, no section rendered.
* build_raw_prompt() (playlist > prompt lines) also receives the prior-task-context section.

Part B:
* Every rendered prompt_bead prompt includes the static `## Orientation` section.
* The section's instructions work in both playlist mode (dirty working tree) and standalone mode (clean tree, work in HEAD) without modification.
* The section appears BEFORE `## Rules` so the agent reads it before starting implementation.
* The section cross-references the `## Prior Task Context` section so agents know to treat it as a claim, not ground truth.

Interaction with ralph-0h1.20:
* PRIOR_TASK_CONTEXT and Orientation apply to ALL bead prompts, including playlist-mode prompts running on a single playlist branch. No conflict.
* Orientation's `git diff` / `git show HEAD` instructions are branch-agnostic — they work on whatever branch the bead lands on.

## Non-goals

* Reading `br close --reason` from the previous bead. The close reason is written AFTER the agent closes the bead — by the time Part A runs (in handle_task_outcome), the reason is already on the bead, so we *could* pull it via `br show <prev> | jq .reason` instead of stream-log tailing. A follow-up bead can explore that if the stream-log approach proves unreliable. For now, the stream log is authoritative because it captures the agent's own words without a round-trip through the br CLI.
* Walking sibling beads in the parent epic. Only the immediately-prior bead's context is passed forward. Richer epic-wide context can be added later if a pilot run shows it would help.
close_reason: VERIFY: Source lib/loader.sh, set LAST_TASK_ID/LAST_TASK_SUMMARY, call format_prior_task_context — should render ## Prior Task Context section. Empty globals should produce empty string. Run extract_last_assistant_text on a stream log. NOTES: Part A (claimed summary) extracts from stream-json, injected via {{PRIOR_TASK_CONTEXT}} in prompt_bead.txt and prompt_raw.txt. Part B (orientation) is static in prompt_bead.txt. Globals cleared after prompt build.

title: Gate template expansion in playlist authoring
description:
Report ref: §2.11. Depends on: ralph-0h1.9 (gate template system).

Injects #TAG shorthand lines into playlist files during authoring. Tags are NOT expanded here — they stay as shorthand and get expanded at runtime (task 9). Injected gate prompts instruct Claude to create only fix beads (type=bug), not feature work.

## V1 Self-Healing Constraints

Gate template prompts include instructions that constrain what Claude can inject:
* Only beads of type=bug can be created during self-healing
* No new feature work, refactoring, or scope expansion from gate prompts
* This keeps the self-healing loop focused on fixing what's broken, not evolving the plan

These constraints are enforced by the template text itself (instructions to Claude), not by ralph code. The hard injection limit (separate task) provides the safety net.

## Implementation

* In lib/gates.sh, add playlist_inject_gates():
  * Takes a playlist file path as input
  * Reads the file line by line, tracking:
    * Bead count since last gate
    * Current epic (parent of current bead, via br show)
    * Whether a #SMOKE_TEST has appeared yet
  * Insertion rules:
    * Every ~5 beads without a gate: insert "> #COMPLETENESS_SCAN" line
    * At epic boundaries (parent epic changes): insert ">@opus #REVIEW" line
    * After first 5 beads if no #SMOKE_TEST exists: insert ">@opus #SMOKE_TEST" line
  * Inserted lines are bare #TAG shorthand — no user context. Claude adds context during semantic validation (task 13), or the user adds it manually.
  * Write the augmented playlist back to the file
  * Return count of gates injected

* Called by:
  * playlist_validate_semantic() (task 13) — injects missing gates during init
  * playlist_create() (task 14) — injects gates as post-creation pass

Acceptance criteria:
* playlist_inject_gates() inserts bare #TAG lines at correct intervals
* Completeness scans every ~5 beads without a gate
* Review prompts at epic boundaries
* Smoke test after first 5 beads if missing
* Tags are shorthand only — NOT expanded in the file
* Template text constrains self-healing to bug-type beads only
* Reusable by both init and create flows
* Returns count of injected gates
close_reason: Gate injection function added to gates.sh with epic boundary detection and density-based insertion

title: Validation marker check on playlist startup
description:
Report ref: §2.12 Path A. Depends on: ralph-0h1.12 (syntax validation).

When ralph --playlist FILE is invoked, check for a validation marker. If absent, warn and offer options. The fallback only offers Phase 1 (syntax validation) until Phase 2 (semantic, task 13) is implemented — this avoids a broken code path.

Implementation:
* In lib/playlist.sh playlist_init(), after loading the file into PLAYLIST_LINES:
  * Scan first 5 lines for a line matching: # ✓ VALIDATED:
  * If found: log "Playlist validated: <marker line>" and continue
  * If not found and not DRY_RUN:
    * Print warning:
      [ralph] WARNING: Playlist not validated.
        Missing: quality gates, API verification, completeness scan
        Run 'ralph playlist init $PLAYLIST' to validate and add quality gates.
        Continue anyway? [y/N]
    * Read user input:
      * y or Y: continue (log "Proceeding without validation")
      * n or N or empty:
        * Check if playlist_validate_semantic function exists (Phase 2 implemented):
          * If yes: offer full init: "Run 'ralph playlist init $PLAYLIST' now? [Y/n]"
            * Y: run playlist_validate_syntax then playlist_validate_semantic, reload, continue
            * n: exit 1
          * If no (Phase 2 not yet implemented): offer syntax-only:
            "Run syntax validation on $PLAYLIST? [Y/n]"
            * Y: run playlist_validate_syntax only, continue (no marker added — that's Phase 2's job)
            * n: exit 1
    * Non-interactive (no TTY): skip prompt, log warning, continue.
  * If DRY_RUN: log warning, don't prompt.

Acceptance criteria:
* Playlist with "# ✓ VALIDATED:" in first 5 lines proceeds without warning
* Playlist without marker shows warning and prompts
* y continues without validation
* n offers inline init (full if Phase 2 exists, syntax-only otherwise)
* Non-interactive skips prompt with warning
* Dry-run logs warning only
* No broken code path if Phase 2 (task 13) isn't implemented yet

## Interaction with ralph-0h1.20

Use the shared helper playlist_scan_directives() introduced by ralph-0h1.20 instead of rolling a second independent scanner for the "# ✓ VALIDATED:" marker. The helper walks leading comments (before the first actionable line) and returns a dictionary of "# key: value" pairs. The validation marker is just another key in that dict, alongside "branch" from ralph-0h1.20. Two scanners on the same leading-comment region would drift over time.

Recommended shape: playlist_init() calls playlist_scan_directives() once and stores the result in a global associative array PLAYLIST_HEADER. Both features then read from it:
* ralph-0h1.20 reads PLAYLIST_HEADER[branch] for the in-file branch override.
* This bead (ralph-0h1.11) reads PLAYLIST_HEADER[validated] for the marker check.

Note: "# ✓ VALIDATED: <timestamp>" uses a slightly different shape than "# <key>: <value>" — if playlist_scan_directives() treats it as key="✓ VALIDATED" value="<timestamp>", normalise in the consumer rather than adding special cases to the scanner.
close_reason: VERIFY: Playlist without '# ✓ VALIDATED:' in first 5 lines shows warning and prompts. With marker, proceeds silently. Dry-run logs warning only. Non-TTY continues without prompt. NOTES: lib/playlist_marker.sh (check_validation_marker, prompt_for_validation, offer_inline_init). Called from playlist_init().

title: ralph playlist init — syntax validation phase
description:
Report ref: §2.12 Path C, Phase 1. This is the deterministic phase of ralph playlist init.

Add a ralph playlist init <file> subcommand. Phase 1 validates syntax AND gate density deterministically — no Claude invocation. Phase 2 (task 13, semantic validation via Claude) runs automatically if Phase 1 passes.

Implementation:
* In lib/args.sh parse_args(), detect "playlist" as first arg followed by "init":
  * ralph playlist init <file> — set PLAYLIST_INIT_MODE=true, PLAYLIST=<file>
  * After parse_args, if PLAYLIST_INIT_MODE, call playlist_validate_syntax. If it passes, call playlist_validate_semantic (task 13). Then exit.

* In lib/playlist.sh, add playlist_validate_syntax():
  Two sub-phases, both deterministic:

  **Phase 1a: Line-by-line syntax**
  * Read the playlist file line by line
  * For each non-blank, non-comment line:
    * If starts with ">": valid prompt line, no further check needed
    * Otherwise: treat as bead ID. Run br show "$line" --json 2>/dev/null
      * If br show fails (exit non-zero): ERROR — "$line" is not a valid bead ID or prompt
      * If br show succeeds but status is "closed" or "done": WARNING — bead "$line" is already closed
  * Track error_count and warning_count

  **Phase 1b: Gate density analysis**
  * Call gate_check_playlist() from lib/gates.sh (task 9) to analyze gate presence
  * Call gate_minimum_rules() to enforce requirements:
    * Zero gates in a playlist with >1 bead = ERROR (blocks)
    * Low density (fewer than 1 gate per 7 beads) = WARNING
    * Missing #COMPLETENESS_SCAN (none per 10 beads or per epic) = WARNING
    * Missing #SMOKE_TEST (none and playlist has >5 beads) = WARNING
    * Missing #REVIEW (none at epic boundaries) = WARNING
  * Gate errors are added to error_count, gate warnings to warning_count

  **Report:**
  [ralph] Syntax validation:
    Line 15: ERROR — "chippie ogz3.1" is not a valid bead ID or prompt
    Line 41: WARNING — bead "chippie-xyz.99" does not exist in beads

  Gate analysis:
    Beads: 39  |  Gates: 0  |  Density: 0:39
    ERROR: No quality gates found. Every playlist needs at least 1 gate.
    WARNING: No #SMOKE_TEST found. Recommend API validation after foundation beads.
    WARNING: No #COMPLETENESS_SCAN found. Recommend TODO/FIXME scan every 10 beads.

    3 errors, 2 warnings. Fix errors before proceeding.

  * Exit 1 if errors > 0. Exit 0 if only warnings or clean.
  * If exit 0: Phase 2 (task 13) runs automatically — Claude adds missing gates, verifies endpoints, adds validation marker.

Acceptance criteria:
* ralph playlist init foo.playlist validates line syntax AND gate density
* Invalid bead IDs and zero gates are errors (block Phase 2)
* Low density and missing gate types are warnings (don't block)
* Gate analysis uses gate_check_playlist() and gate_minimum_rules() from task 9
* Phase 2 (semantic, task 13) runs automatically on Phase 1 success
* From user perspective: one command does both phases
* Exit code 1 on errors, 0 on clean/warnings-only

## Interaction with ralph-0h1.20

Phase 1a must recognise "# branch: NAME" as a valid directive, not flag it as a stray comment. Add a new validation rule to Phase 1a:

* Scan leading comments (before the first actionable line) for directives of the form "# <key>: <value>" using the shared playlist_scan_directives() helper from ralph-0h1.20.
* For the "branch" key specifically:
  * Run git check-ref-format --branch "NAME" to validate the name is a legal git ref.
  * Illegal branch name (spaces, "..", leading "-", control chars, etc.) → ERROR: 'Line N: invalid branch name "NAME" (git check-ref-format failed)'.
  * Duplicate "# branch:" directives in the leading comment block → ERROR: 'Line N: duplicate "# branch:" directive — precedence is ambiguous'.
* A "# branch:" directive appearing AFTER the first actionable line → WARNING: 'Line N: "# branch:" directive after first actionable line will be ignored at runtime (branch is resolved from leading comments only)'.

Do NOT re-implement precedence (CLI > file > default) in the validator — that logic lives in playlist_resolve_branch(). Phase 1a only validates that any directive present is syntactically sound and unambiguous. The rest of the syntax validator (bead IDs, > prompts, gate density) is unchanged.
close_reason: VERIFY: ralph playlist init /tmp/test.playlist — should validate line syntax (bead IDs against br) and gate density (gate_check_playlist + gate_minimum_rules). Invalid beads and zero gates are errors (exit 1). Closed beads are warnings. Branch directives validated for git ref format. NOTES: lib/playlist_init.sh (run_playlist_init, validate_line_syntax, validate_gate_density), args.sh subcommand parsing.

title: ralph playlist init — semantic validation phase
description:
Report ref: §2.12 Path C, Phase 2. Depends on: ralph-0h1.12 (syntax validation), ralph-0h1.10 (gate template expansion).

Phase 2 of ralph playlist init. Runs automatically after Phase 1 (syntax + gate density) passes. First injects missing gate #TAG shorthand lines deterministically, then invokes Claude to add context to those tags and audit bead descriptions.

Implementation:
* In lib/playlist.sh, add playlist_validate_semantic(). Called automatically by Phase 1 on success.

  **Step 1: Deterministic gate injection**
  * Call playlist_inject_gates() from lib/gates.sh (task 10) to insert missing #TAG shorthand lines at appropriate intervals.
  * Log how many gates were injected. E.g. "Injected 3 gates: 1 #SMOKE_TEST, 1 #REVIEW, 1 #COMPLETENESS_SCAN"

  **Step 2: Claude semantic audit**
  * Gather context:
    * Playlist file contents (now including injected #TAG lines from step 1)
    * For each bead ID: br show <id> --json (title + description)
    * Project .ralph/config contents (if exists)
    * List of key files in the project
  * Build a prompt for Claude with instructions:
    You are validating a ralph playlist file. #TAG shorthand lines have been auto-inserted.
    Audit and improve:
    1. Add context to bare #TAG lines. For example, change:
         >@opus #SMOKE_TEST
       to:
         >@opus #SMOKE_TEST curl POST /api/v1/auth/login, verify token, test GET /clients with token
       The context should be specific to what was implemented in the surrounding beads.
    2. Verify each bead description against the real codebase:
       * curl every API endpoint referenced (if backend is running)
       * Check that file paths in descriptions exist
       * Flag fabricated URLs or nonexistent endpoints
       * Update bead descriptions via br update where wrong
    3. Check for missing backend dependencies — create backend beads if needed
    4. Add validation marker: # ✓ VALIDATED: <timestamp> by ralph playlist init
    5. Print a report of every change made
  * Call invoke_claude with this prompt
  * Log: "Playlist validation complete. Review changes with: git diff $PLAYLIST"

Acceptance criteria:
* Phase 2 runs automatically after Phase 1 passes
* playlist_inject_gates() (task 10) inserts bare #TAG shorthand lines first
* Claude adds project-specific context to the bare tags
* Claude can verify endpoints, update bead descriptions, create backend beads
* Validation marker is added to line 1
* Changes are visible via git diff
* If Claude invocation fails, log warning and exit (don't corrupt the file)
close_reason: Phase 2 semantic validation implemented: gate injection, Claude audit for context/descriptions, validation marker

title: ralph playlist create from beads/epics
description:
Report ref: §2.12 Path B. Depends on: ralph-0h1.12 (syntax validation), ralph-0h1.10 (gate injection).

Add ralph playlist create subcommand. Creates the playlist then pipes through init for verification — avoids duplicating curl verification in both create and init.

Implementation:
* In lib/args.sh parse_args(), detect "playlist" as first arg followed by "create":
  * ralph playlist create <id1> <id2> ... -o <output-file>
  * ralph playlist create --epic <epic-id> -o <output-file>
  * ralph playlist create --epic <id1> --epic <id2> -o <output-file>
  * Set PLAYLIST_CREATE_MODE=true, collect bead IDs or epic IDs, set OUTPUT_FILE

* In lib/playlist.sh, add playlist_create():

  **Step 1: Gather bead details**
  * If --epic flags: expand to children via br ready --parent=<id> -r --json in dependency order.
  * If raw bead IDs: use as-is.
  * For each bead: br show <id> --json for title + description.

  **Step 2: Claude generates playlist structure**
  * Build creation prompt focused on ORDERING and STRUCTURE only:
    * Order beads by dependency
    * Place #TAG gate lines at appropriate intervals with context
    * Flag any bead descriptions that reference endpoints, URLs, or file paths (but don't verify — init does that)
    * Write to $OUTPUT_FILE
  * Call invoke_claude

  **Step 3: Pipe through init for verification**
  * Run playlist_validate_syntax() (task 12) — syntax + gate density check
  * If Phase 2 available: run playlist_validate_semantic() (task 13) — Claude verifies endpoints, refines gates, adds marker
  * This avoids duplicating the curl/verification logic in both create and init
  * Log: "Playlist created: $OUTPUT_FILE (N beads, M gates, P prompts)"

Acceptance criteria:
* ralph playlist create <ids> -o out.playlist generates a valid playlist file
* ralph playlist create --epic <id> expands epic children in dependency order
* Multiple --epic flags combine children
* Claude handles ordering and gate placement
* Verification (endpoint checking, bead validation) delegated to init pipeline
* No duplication of curl/verification logic between create and init
* Output reports bead count, gate count, prompt count

## Interaction with ralph-0h1.20

When create is invoked with a SINGLE --epic flag, prepend a "# branch: <epic-slug>.playlist" directive as the FIRST LINE of the generated file. The epic slug is derived via slugify() from the epic title (same helper already used by lib/tasks.sh get_branch_context). This gives operators the sensible default branch for epic-scoped playlists without needing to remember to add the header manually.

Behavior matrix:
* Single --epic flag → emit "# branch: <epic-slug>.playlist" at the top of the generated file.
* Multiple --epic flags → do NOT emit a branch directive. Fall through to ralph-0h1.20's filename-derived default at run time.
* Raw bead IDs (no --epic) → do NOT emit a branch directive. Filename-derived default applies.

The emitted directive is a hint, not a lock — operators can still override at run time with ralph --playlist <file> --playlist-branch NAME. Per ralph-0h1.20 precedence, CLI > in-file header > filename default, so the CLI flag always wins.

Step 2's creation prompt should also be updated to tell Claude NOT to insert any branch-related commentary elsewhere in the file (only the leading directive, which the shell wrapper emits — not Claude).
close_reason: Playlist create subcommand implemented with bead/epic gathering, Claude ordering, gate injection, and init validation pipeline

title: Cost tracking in state
description:
Report ref: R10.

Track cumulative cost across the session. Parse cost from each stream-json log's result entry and maintain a running total in .ralph/state. Add a MAX_COST_USD halt threshold to prevent runaway spending (especially relevant with self-healing injection loops).

Implementation:
* In lib/config.sh, add globals:
  * total_cost_usd="0.00"
  * MAX_COST_USD=0 (0 = no limit, set per-project in .ralph/config)
* In lib/utils.sh save_state(), persist total_cost_usd to .ralph/state
* In lib/utils.sh load_state(), restore total_cost_usd from .ralph/state
* In lib/invoke.sh _invoke_claude_once(), after successful invocation:
  * Parse the result entry from $INVOKE_LOG:
    cost=$(tail -5 "$INVOKE_LOG" | jq -r 'select(.type=="result") | .cost_usd // 0' 2>/dev/null)
  * Use awk for floating-point addition:
    total_cost_usd=$(awk "BEGIN {printf \"%.2f\", $total_cost_usd + ${cost:-0}}")
* In the main loop (both standard and playlist mode), after each invocation:
  * If MAX_COST_USD > 0 and total_cost_usd >= MAX_COST_USD:
    * EXIT_REASON="Cost limit reached (\$$total_cost_usd >= \$$MAX_COST_USD)"
    * Break the loop
* In lib/lifecycle.sh cleanup(), add cost to the summary box:
  printf '│  Total cost:      $%-8s\n' "$total_cost_usd"
  If MAX_COST_USD > 0: also show "│  Cost limit:      $MAX_COST_USD"
* In .ralph/config template, add commented example:
  # MAX_COST_USD=100
* Add --max-cost CLI flag in lib/args.sh.

Acceptance criteria:
* total_cost_usd accumulates across invocations within a session
* Value persists in .ralph/state (survives crash + resume)
* Cleanup summary shows total cost
* MAX_COST_USD > 0 halts the run when exceeded
* --max-cost flag works and overrides config
* Cost parsing handles missing/malformed result entries (defaults to 0)
* Cost limit is checked after each invocation, not mid-invocation

title: Playlist progress file
description:
Report ref: R14.

Write .ralph/playlist-progress.md after each task completes. Human-readable status of what's done, what's next, what's blocked. Useful for monitoring without the TUI dashboard.

Implementation:
* In lib/playlist.sh, add playlist_write_progress():
  * Write to .ralph/playlist-progress.md
  * Format:
    # Playlist Progress: <playlist filename>
    Updated: <timestamp>
    ## Status: <completed>/<total> items (N beads, M prompts)
    ## Completed
    * [bead] chippie-ogz3.1 — Title (closed)
    * [prompt] Review changes (@opus)
    ## Next Up
    * [bead] chippie-hweb.1 — Title (ready)
    ## Remaining
    * [bead] chippie-hweb.2 — Title
    * ...
  * Iterate PLAYLIST_LINES, classify each as completed (before playlist_line), next (at playlist_line), or remaining (after).
  * For bead lines, include title from br show --json (cache to avoid repeated lookups).
* Call playlist_write_progress() from save_state() when in playlist mode (after playlist_advance).

Acceptance criteria:
* .ralph/playlist-progress.md is updated after each task completes
* Shows completed, next, and remaining sections
* Includes bead titles and statuses
* Timestamp is current
* File is human-readable in any editor
close_reason: VERIFY: After playlist task execution, .ralph/playlist-progress.md exists with Completed/Next Up/Remaining sections. Bead titles are looked up via br show. title: Pre-computed project summary at session start

title: Hard injection limit for self-healing loops
description:
From external review: self-healing can loop if fixes keep failing. Need a cap on injected beads. When limit reached, two things happen: (1) playlist_reload() becomes a no-op, (2) gate template expansion omits the self-healing injection instructions. Ralph does NOT halt.

## Behavior

When INJECTION_CAPPED=false (normal):
* playlist_reload() re-reads the file after prompt execution (picks up injected lines)
* gate_expand_tag() returns full template text including self-healing instructions ("create beads, insert into playlist")

When INJECTION_CAPPED=true (limit reached):
* playlist_reload() is a no-op — does not re-read the file
* gate_expand_tag() returns a CAPPED variant of the template that omits self-healing instructions. Claude still runs the quality check (curl, grep, review) but is NOT told to create beads or modify the playlist. The gate becomes read-only observation.
* Ralph continues executing all lines already loaded. No halt, no circuit break, no error.

## Implementation

* In lib/config.sh:
  * MAX_INJECTED_BEADS=0 (0 = use default ratio, positive = hard limit)
  * INJECTION_RATIO=0.25 (if MAX_INJECTED_BEADS=0, limit = max(5, floor(total_beads * 0.25)))

* In lib/playlist.sh:
  * Globals: injected_bead_count=0, injection_limit=0, INJECTION_CAPPED=false
  * In playlist_init(): compute injection_limit from config
  * In playlist_reload():
    * If INJECTION_CAPPED: return immediately (no-op, no file read, no log)
    * Else: reload as normal, count new bead lines, add to injected_bead_count
    * If injected_bead_count >= injection_limit after reload:
      * INJECTION_CAPPED=true
      * Log: "Injection limit reached ($injected_bead_count/$injection_limit). Self-healing disabled for remainder of run."

* In lib/gates.sh gate_expand_tag():
  * If INJECTION_CAPPED: return template text WITHOUT the self-healing instruction block (no "create beads with br create, insert IDs into playlist"). The quality check itself still runs — Claude still curls, greps, reviews — but the prompt does not instruct Claude to create or inject anything.
  * Each template in GATE_TEMPLATES should have two variants or a removable section marker so the capped version can cleanly omit the injection instructions.

* Persist injected_bead_count and INJECTION_CAPPED in .ralph/state

Acceptance criteria:
* When capped: playlist_reload() is a no-op (no file read)
* When capped: gate templates omit self-healing instructions (no bead creation, no playlist modification)
* When capped: quality checks still run (curl, grep, review) — gates are observation-only
* Ralph does NOT halt, does NOT break circuit
* Playlist continues with all currently loaded lines
* Default limit: 25% of playlist bead count (minimum 5)
* Hard limit overrides ratio when configured
* Count persists in .ralph/state

Set INJECTION_CAPPED=true, call playlist_reload — should be a no-op. NOTES: GATE_TEMPLATES_CAPPED array in gates.sh, init_injection_limit/check_injection_limit/count_bead_lines in playlist_reload.sh, state persists injected_bead_count and INJECTION_CAPPED.

title: Auto-escalate model after failure
description:
From external review: if a bead fails on sonnet, escalate to opus automatically instead of retrying with the same model.

Currently invoke_claude() retries up to MAX_RETRIES times with the same model. After the first failure, escalate to a more capable model before retrying. This gives the retry a better chance of succeeding without wasting turns on the same capability level.

Implementation:
* In lib/invoke.sh invoke_claude(), after the first failure:
  * If MODEL is "haiku": escalate to "sonnet"
  * If MODEL is "sonnet": escalate to "opus"
  * If MODEL is already "opus": no escalation (retry with opus)
  * Log: "Escalating model: $old_model → $MODEL for retry"
* The escalated model is used for the retry only. After the task completes (success or final failure), restore the original MODEL.
* In lib/config.sh, add:
  * AUTO_ESCALATE=true (default on, can be disabled)
* Model escalation chain: haiku → sonnet → opus → opus (ceiling)
* If the playlist line has a @model annotation, that's the starting model. Escalation still applies from there.
* Log the escalation clearly so cost tracking (task 15) shows why a particular invocation cost more.

Acceptance criteria:
* First failure on haiku retries with sonnet
* First failure on sonnet retries with opus
* Failure on opus retries with opus (no higher to go)
* Original model is restored after the task completes
* AUTO_ESCALATE=false disables this behavior (retries with same model)
* Escalation is logged clearly
* Works with both standard mode and playlist mode
* Works with @model annotations (escalates from the annotated model)

title: One branch per playlist — resolved once at startup
description:
Stop the per-epic branch sprawl observed in the flutter pilot run. In playlist mode, all work must land on a single branch for the whole session — resolved once at startup, then used everywhere.

## Problem

Ralph has two branch mechanisms running in parallel, neither of which is playlist-aware:

1. `ensure_ralph_branch()` in lib/prereqs.sh:59 unconditionally checks out branch `ralph` at startup.
2. `get_branch_context()` in lib/tasks.sh:152 walks each bead's parent epic and returns an epic-scoped branch string (e.g. `epic:ralph-foundation:ralph`). `format_branch_instructions()` in lib/prompt.sh:80 then renders `templates/branch_epic_ralph.txt` which tells Claude to `git checkout -b ralph-<epic-slug>`.

Result: a playlist spanning multiple epics fans out across many feature branches. The flutter pilot produced this sprawl. Playlist mode is inherently linear execution — it should land on exactly one branch.

## Desired Behavior

When `--playlist FILE` is set, every task (bead OR raw prompt) in the session runs on the same branch, resolved once during `initialize()` using this precedence:

1. CLI flag: `--playlist-branch NAME` (highest priority)
2. In-file directive: a `# branch: NAME` comment appearing BEFORE the first actionable line of the playlist
3. Default: derived from the playlist filename — strip extension, append `.playlist` (e.g. `flutter.playlist` → `flutter.playlist`; `foo.txt` → `foo.playlist`; `bar` → `bar.playlist`)

Standalone (non-playlist) mode is unchanged — keeps existing epic-aware branching.

## Implementation

### lib/config.sh
* Add `PLAYLIST_BRANCH=""` — the resolved branch name for the current playlist session. Empty means non-playlist mode.

### lib/args.sh
* Add `--playlist-branch NAME` flag, stored in a new global `PLAYLIST_BRANCH_CLI` (NOT `PLAYLIST_BRANCH` — the CLI value is an *input* to resolution, not the resolved result).
* Reject `--playlist-branch` without `--playlist` in `validate_playlist_args()` with a clear error.
* Document in `show_help()`.

### lib/playlist.sh
* Add `playlist_resolve_branch()` — runs the precedence chain and sets the global `PLAYLIST_BRANCH`. Called from `initialize()` after `parse_args` and before `ensure_ralph_branch`.
  1. If `PLAYLIST_BRANCH_CLI` is non-empty → use it.
  2. Else scan `$PLAYLIST` line-by-line until the first non-comment, non-blank line. Among the comments seen, look for `# branch: NAME` (case-insensitive key, trimmed value). If found → use it.
  3. Else derive from `$(basename "$PLAYLIST")`: strip the final extension with `${name%.*}`, append `.playlist`.
* Extract the directive scanner into its own helper `playlist_scan_directives()` so it can grow to handle other `# key: value` headers later without bloating the resolver.
* Log the resolved value: `log "Playlist branch: ${C_BOLD_CYAN}$PLAYLIST_BRANCH${C_RESET}"`.

### lib/prereqs.sh
* Extract the shared create-or-checkout logic into `checkout_or_create_branch()` taking the branch name as an argument. Keep `ensure_ralph_branch()` as a one-line wrapper that calls it with `ralph` — backward compatible.
* Add `ensure_playlist_branch()` that calls `checkout_or_create_branch "$PLAYLIST_BRANCH"`.

### lib/lifecycle.sh (initialize)
* After `parse_args`, if `$PLAYLIST` is set: call `playlist_resolve_branch` BEFORE `ensure_ralph_branch`.
* Replace the unconditional `ensure_ralph_branch` call with a guard: if `$PLAYLIST_BRANCH` is non-empty → `ensure_playlist_branch`, else → `ensure_ralph_branch`.
* Current ordering keeps `playlist_init` after branch setup — fine, but `playlist_resolve_branch` must come BEFORE `ensure_playlist_branch`.

### lib/tasks.sh (get_branch_context)
* Add a guard at the top: if `$PLAYLIST_BRANCH` is non-empty, return `playlist:$PLAYLIST_BRANCH` and skip the epic walk entirely. This is the single choke point — all downstream branch logic keys off this return value.

### lib/prompt.sh (format_branch_instructions)
* Add a new case `playlist:*` that extracts the branch name and renders `templates/branch_playlist.txt`.

### templates/branch_playlist.txt (new file)
* Tell Claude: you are working on branch `{{BRANCH}}`; do NOT create feature branches; do NOT run `git checkout` to any other branch; commit directly here; merging is a separate manual step.

### Dry-run
* `playlist_dry_run_summary()` in lib/playlist.sh should print the resolved branch at the top of the plan so operators see it before committing.

### Docs
* Update CLAUDE.md "Playlist Mode" section to explain the single-branch rule and precedence.
* Update CLAUDE.md "Branch Strategy" to document that epic-based branch selection is bypassed in playlist mode.

## Acceptance Criteria

* `ralph --playlist flutter.playlist` — every task executes on branch `flutter.playlist`; no `ralph-<epic-slug>` branches are created.
* `ralph --playlist foo.playlist --playlist-branch custom` — every task executes on branch `custom`.
* A playlist file whose first non-blank, non-actionable lines include `# branch: shiny` resolves to branch `shiny` UNLESS `--playlist-branch` is passed (CLI wins).
* A `# branch: X` directive AFTER the first actionable line is treated as a normal comment and ignored.
* A playlist file named `bar.txt` (no `.playlist` extension) resolves to branch `bar.playlist` by default.
* `--playlist-branch` without `--playlist` fails with a clear error.
* Standalone mode (no `--playlist`): `get_branch_context()` still returns epic-aware contexts; `ensure_ralph_branch()` still runs. No regression.
* Dry-run (`--dry-run --playlist FILE`) prints the resolved branch name at the top of the plan.
* The Claude prompt for any task in playlist mode instructs it NOT to create or switch branches.
* Logged at startup: the resolved branch and its source (cli / file / default) so operators can debug precedence.

## Non-goals

* Remote mode (`--remote`) integration — out of scope; handle in a follow-up if needed.
* Auto-creating the branch from a specific base other than current HEAD or `WORKING_BRANCH` — keep existing semantics.
* Multi-branch playlists (a playlist that intentionally spans branches). Explicit non-goal: one playlist = one branch.

Claude prompt says no branch switching. NOTES: playlist_branch.sh (resolve+scan), prereqs.sh (checkout_or_create_branch), tasks.sh guard, prompt.sh playlist:* case, branch_playlist.txt template.

title: Gate templates: #REFACTOR and #DOCUMENT for post-epic workflow
description:
Depends on: ralph-0h1.9 (gate template system must exist first).

Add two new gate templates to GATE_TEMPLATES in lib/gates.sh that mirror the user's ~/.claude/commands/refactor.md and ~/.claude/commands/document.md slash command workflows, adapted for autonomous playlist execution (no interactive approval gates).

## Why These Templates

The existing gate templates (#SMOKE_TEST, #COMPLETENESS_SCAN, #REVIEW) are tactical mid-run checks. The user's core workflow after completing a major feature is:
1. Fresh session → /refactor (systematic cleanup)
2. Fresh session → /document (update docs/INDEX.md, feature docs, ADRs)

These should be available as playlist gate tags so playlist authors can place them at epic boundaries or playlist tail. They are heavier than existing gates — designed for end-of-epic or end-of-playlist placement, not every 5 beads.

## Template Definitions

### #REFACTOR

Adapted from ~/.claude/commands/refactor.md. Key adaptations for autonomous mode:
* No "WAIT for user approval" — execute the full cycle
* Scope = git diff from playlist start (not uncommitted changes, since ralph commits per-task)
* Phase 1 (Analysis): git diff --stat from session start, read modified files, search for existing patterns/utilities, identify structural violations (200+ line files, 50+ line functions, SRP, DRY), critical code review (reinvented wheels, logic errors, edge cases, security, error handling, performance, type safety, incomplete implementations)
* Phase 2 (Plan): Write plan to SCRATCHPAD.md with Must Fix / Should Fix / Consider categories, reuse opportunities, structural changes, deletions, risk assessment
* Phase 3 (Execute): One logical change at a time, run tests after each, checkpoint after logical units
* Priority order: security/logic fixes → secondary issues → replace reinvented code → delete dead code → extract duplicates → split monoliths → rename for clarity → align architecture → simplify
* Constraints: No new features. No premature abstractions. Bug-type beads only for issues that can't be fixed in-session. Delete SCRATCHPAD.md when done.

Template text should be ~15 lines capturing this workflow as direct instructions to Claude.

### #DOCUMENT

Adapted from ~/.claude/commands/document.md. Key adaptations for autonomous mode:
* No "WAIT for user approval" — execute the full cycle
* Scope = all changes in the playlist session (git log/diff from session branch point)
* Phase 1 (Analyze): Identify changed files from git, check docs/INDEX.md structure, scan for orphaned docs, read implementation files
* Phase 2 (Plan): Assess what needs creating/updating, identify orphans, list sections to write — write plan to SCRATCHPAD.md
* Phase 3 (Write): Create/update feature docs following the template structure (frontmatter with tracks/status/last_updated, Overview, How It Works, Implementation with architecture + key components table + key functions, Configuration, Usage Examples, Related Docs, Edge Cases), update docs/INDEX.md (quick reference table + categorized listing + maintenance log), create ADRs for significant design decisions
* Orphan handling: Index valid unlisted docs, flag duplicates for consolidation
* Constraints: INDEX.md is mandatory. Consolidate over create. Practical focus. Code references with file paths. No filler. Bidirectional links. Delete SCRATCHPAD.md when done.

Template text should be ~15 lines capturing this workflow as direct instructions to Claude.

## Integration with gate_inject_gates() (ralph-0h1.10)

Update playlist_inject_gates() insertion rules:
* #REFACTOR: inject once at the END of the playlist (after last bead/prompt). Never mid-run.
* #DOCUMENT: inject once at the END of the playlist, AFTER #REFACTOR. Never mid-run.
* These are only injected if the playlist has >5 beads (skip for trivial playlists).
* Both use @opus model override by default when auto-injected.

This means a playlist tail auto-generated by inject_gates would look like:
```
>@opus #REFACTOR
>@opus #DOCUMENT
```

## Acceptance Criteria

* GATE_TEMPLATES contains REFACTOR and DOCUMENT entries
* gate_expand_tag() handles both new tags
* gate_is_valid_tag() recognizes both
* Template text captures the essential multi-phase workflow without interactive approval
* #REFACTOR scopes to session git diff, not uncommitted changes
* #DOCUMENT creates/updates docs/INDEX.md and feature docs with proper frontmatter
* Both constrain Claude to bug-type beads only for discovered issues
* playlist_inject_gates() appends both at playlist tail (>5 beads only)
* Auto-injected lines use @opus model override
* gate_minimum_rules() updated: #REFACTOR and #DOCUMENT recommended once per playlist (WARNING if missing at tail, not ERROR)
* Existing gate behavior unchanged
